summary: This component displays a Bluesky engagement section for a blog article. It fetches data about whether the article has been posted to Bluesky and how many people have engaged with it, then shows either a 'share this article' prompt or an engagement counter with likes and comments. The component carefully handles loading and error states to avoid showing misleading messages to the user.

explanations.10: This is a helper function that generates the right headline text based on whether we found a Bluesky post for this article and how many people have engaged with it.
explanations.28: The comment explains why we use the same generic 'join the conversation' message both when data is still loading and when it fails to load — we never want to mislead users by saying 'no one has engaged yet' when we might just not know.
explanations.42: The comment notes that we're using two completely different translated sentences for singular vs plural (not just changing a verb), because some languages like French have agreement rules that affect more than just the verb form.
explanations.67: This hook tries to find a Bluesky post for this article by looking through the account's post history, or uses a manually specified record key from the article's metadata if one was provided.
explanations.68: We're creating a modified copy of the metadata object where we fill in the discovered record key, so downstream components can see whether a post was found.
explanations.77: We return null (render nothing) while still searching for a matching Bluesky post, to avoid showing a 'Share on Bluesky' button that would disappear once we find the post.
explanations.97: We only show the engagement UI (likes, comments, link to post) if the data loaded successfully; if the post was deleted or unreachable, we hide this entire section to avoid showing a broken link.
